correctness.rationale: For each fixed normal, planar convexity gives a concave chord-length profile on its support; central symmetry makes its zero extension even and nonincreasing on the nonnegative half-line. Centering thus maximizes the area over all translations. In vertex-normal coordinates the nonnegative projected vertex levels are 0, a and 1; their chord lengths are 2, 2a and 0. For edge-normal coordinates the relevant levels are 0, d and c; the chord lengths are 2c, 2c and 2d, the last at the support edge. Integrating the linear pieces gives the four stated caps, with area ordering opposite to cap ordering. For D=C_E-C_V, the initial linear factor after dividing by s is strictly decreasing with D(d)<0; D(d)<0<D(a) selects the upper zero of the convex middle polynomial; D(a)>0>D(c) selects the upper zero of the concave last polynomial. At s=1/2+d both last-interval caps reduce to a-c+1/4, using c=(1+sqrt(2))d and c^2-d^2=a. The exact signs follow from the frozen radical enclosures by rational substitution; an independent Decimal calculation gave endpoint differences -0.0024000882, 0.0057943256, -0.0139887394 and reproduced all three quoted full widths. The zero-width plank has zero area; E alone saturates for 2c<=W<2 and both saturate from W=2. No unrestricted direction optimum is required.
residual_risks: Decimal check is corroboration, not a certificate. The packaged counter increments even when a sampled sign is skipped near a root; the universal sign proof does not rely on that count.
